title: Two ways to upgrade a feeder, as big-M rows

blocks.text: A feeder that keeps tripping is upgraded in exactly one of two ways. A **line crew** reconductors the worst spans: it spends between 10 and 30 ($k), and the capacity it adds is at most half of what it spends. A **rebuild** replaces the feeder: it spends between 60 and 100, and adds at most 40 of capacity, whatever it spends.

`mode_variables` (given) creates the spend $`s \in [10, 100]`$, the capacity gain $`g \in [0, 40]`$ and the binary $`r`$ (1 = rebuild, 0 = line crew). Write `add_bigm_modes(model, s, g, r)` in `upgrade.py`: the disjunction as big-M rows, each with the smallest $`M`$ the variables' bounds justify, computed in code from `s.lower_bound`, `g.upper_bound` and the module's constants.

"From the bounds" means from $`10 \le s \le 100`$ and $`0 \le g \le 40`$ alone, as in the variable-bounds rule of lesson 6.2.1, and not from the other rows of the disjunct. For the line crew's gain row, the reference takes the largest value $`g - 0.5\,s`$ can reach over those bounds, $`40 - 0.5 \cdot 10 = 35`$. It does not use the rebuild's own floor $`s \ge 60`$, which would bring that $`M`$ down to 10; that smaller value is also valid, and the tests accept it, but it is a step beyond the bounds.
Some rows of each disjunct are already implied by the variables' bounds, and need no row of their own. Decide which, write the remaining rows with their $`M`$s in this notation first, then code them.

The tests fix a plan by its variables' bounds and ask the solver whether it is allowed, so any correct set of rows passes; one more test checks that the LP relaxation of your rows is at least as tight as rows with $`M`$s from the bounds. About six lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

LINE_CREW = (10, 30)      # $k a line-crew upgrade may spend; its capacity gain is at most half the spend
REBUILD = (60, 100)       # $k a rebuild may spend; its gain is at most 40 (the gain variable's bound)
GAIN_PER_DOLLAR = 0.5


def mode_variables(model: mathopt.Model, integer: bool = True):
    """Spend s, capacity gain g, and r = 1 if the feeder is rebuilt, 0 if a line crew upgrades it."""
    s = model.add_variable(lb=LINE_CREW[0], ub=REBUILD[1], name="spend")
    g = model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=40, name="gain")
    r = model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=1, is_integer=integer, name="rebuild")
    return s, g, r


def add_bigm_modes(model: mathopt.Model, s, g, r) -> None:
    """Line crew (r = 0) or rebuild (r = 1), as big-M rows with M from the variables' bounds."""
    m_cap = s.upper_bound - LINE_CREW[1]
    m_gain = g.upper_bound - GAIN_PER_DOLLAR * s.lower_bound
    m_floor = REBUILD[0] - s.lower_bound
    model.add_linear_constraint(s <= LINE_CREW[1] + m_cap * r, name="line_spend_cap")
    model.add_linear_constraint(g <= GAIN_PER_DOLLAR * s + m_gain * r, name="line_gain")
    model.add_linear_constraint(s >= REBUILD[0] - m_floor * (1 - r), name="rebuild_spend_floor")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = mathopt.Model()
    s, g, r = mode_variables(model)
    add_bigm_modes(model, s, g, r)
    model.maximize(3 * g - s)
    print(mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS).objective_value())

cases.says: a line-crew upgrade gaining half its spend is allowed, and one gaining more refused
a line-crew upgrade spending 30 is allowed and one spending 40 refused
a rebuild spending less than 60 is refused
a rebuild may gain 40 on a spend of 60, which a line crew may not
the LP bound with your Ms is no looser than Ms from the variables' bounds give

origin.section: A Disjunction Written as Big-M Switches Each Disjunct With Its Own Binary

concepts: each disjunct of an either-or rule gets a switch, and each row's M comes from the bounds
a disjunct's row that the variables' bounds already imply needs no switched row
